stem:
Farhan throws a ball straight up. The ball slows, stops briefly, then falls and speeds up as it comes down.

Which claims correctly explain the motion? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Earth pulls the ball toward itself while the ball goes up and while it comes down.
Earth's pull makes the ball slow on the way up and speed up on the way down.
An upward force from the throw stays inside the ball until it runs out; Earth pulls only after the ball starts falling.
Earth pushes the ball upward the whole time the ball is rising.

teacher.key_rationale: Earth's gravitational pull acts toward Earth throughout the flight, so the ball slows going up and speeds up coming down. The throw does not leave a lasting upward force inside the ball, and Earth does not push the ball upward while it rises.
